statements.label: supported
statements.text: Duplicated soybean gene pairs showed widely varied transcriptional profiles, both inside individual tissues and between different tissues.
statements.evidence: Our analysis revealed extensive diversity of transcriptional profiles within and across tissues among duplicated gene pairs.
statements.note: The abstract reports extensive diversity of transcriptional profiles among duplicated gene pairs, both within and across tissues.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For duplicated soybean genes, divergence across tissues was more likely driven by changing ACR accessibility between tissues than by sequence variation in the ACRs.
statements.evidence: Within-tissue divergence was largely attributable to genetic variation in their associated accessible chromatin regions (ACRs), where cis-regulatory elements reside, whereas cross-tissue divergence was more likely shaped by dynamics in ACR chromatin accessibility profiles across tissues.
statements.note: The abstract ties within-tissue divergence to genetic variation in ACRs, whereas cross-tissue divergence was more likely shaped by changes in ACR accessibility across tissues.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Deleting candidate cell-type-specific ACRs by genome editing abolished cell-type-specific expression of the linked duplicated soybean genes.
statements.evidence: Finally, we traced the evolution of cell-type-specific expression and cell-type-specific ACRs within duplicated gene sets, illustrating a powerful framework for identifying candidate regulatory regions driving cell-type-specific expression.
statements.note: The abstract offers a framework for identifying candidate regulatory regions but reports no genome editing or other functional test of those ACRs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In gene sets from soybean's two whole-genome duplications, the majority of ACRs kept at least one duplicated counterpart sequence that gradually accumulated mutations.
statements.evidence: we found that most ACRs retained one or multiple corresponding duplicated sequences in which mutations gradually accumulated over time, while a subset likely arose de novo
statements.note: The abstract states that most ACRs retained one or multiple duplicated counterpart sequences in which mutations accumulated gradually over time.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Expression-level dominance in natural Capsella allotetraploids was driven mainly by differences in DNA methylation between the two parental subgenomes.
statements.evidence: In conclusion, both short- and long-term mechanisms contributed to transcriptomic and phenotypic changes in natural allotetraploids.
statements.note: The abstract never examines DNA methylation; the only mechanism it names is homoeologous synapsis, as the source of homoeolog expression bias.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the expression-level dominance cases seen in natural Capsella allotetraploids, 40% also occurred in resynthesized allotetraploids.
statements.evidence: However, short-term changes mattered, and 40% of the cases of ELD in natural allotetraploids were already observed in resynthesized allotetraploids.
statements.note: The abstract reports that 40% of ELD cases in natural allotetraploids were already observed in resynthesized allotetraploids.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with resynthesized allotetraploids, natural Capsella allotetraploids showed more expression-level dominance toward the self-fertilizing parental species.
statements.evidence: Natural allotetraploids also had more ELD toward the self-fertilizing parental species than resynthesized allotetraploids, mirroring the establishment of the selfing syndrome.
statements.note: The abstract states that natural allotetraploids had more ELD toward the self-fertilizing parent than resynthesized allotetraploids.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Homoeolog expression bias in resynthesized Capsella allotetraploids varied strikingly across chromosomes and individuals, arising mainly from homoeologous synapsis.
statements.evidence: Resynthesized allotetraploids showed striking variation of HEB among chromosomes and individuals. Homoeologous synapsis was its primary source
statements.note: The abstract reports striking HEB variation among chromosomes and individuals in resynthesized allotetraploids and names homoeologous synapsis as its primary source.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The new Brassica carinata genome assembly is chromosome-scale, spans 1.31 Gbp and was generated with 156.9-fold sequencing coverage.
statements.evidence: Here, we report a chromosome scale 1.31-Gbp genome assembly with 156.9-fold sequencing coverage for B. carinata
statements.note: The abstract reports a chromosome-scale 1.31-Gbp assembly of B. carinata built with 156.9-fold sequencing coverage.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Analysis of the B. carinata genome revealed an expansion of transcription factor networks and of agronomically important gene families.
statements.evidence: Notably, we identified an expansion of transcription factor networks and agronomically important gene families.
statements.note: The abstract states that an expansion of transcription factor networks and agronomically important gene families was identified.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Having all Triangle of U reference genomes allowed the study to examine subgenome dominance in the domestication and continued improvement of B. carinata and other Brassicas.
statements.evidence: Completion of the Triangle of U comparative genomics platform has allowed us to examine the dynamics of polyploid evolution and the role of subgenome dominance in the domestication and continuing agronomic improvement of B. carinata and other Brassica species.
statements.note: The abstract says completing the Triangle of U platform allowed examination of the role of subgenome dominance in domestication and agronomic improvement.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Brassica carinata harbors less genetic diversity than the other two allotetraploid species of the Triangle of U.
statements.evidence: Of the genomes of these species, that of B. carinata is the least understood.
statements.note: That sentence concerns how well the genome is understood, not genetic diversity; the abstract never compares diversity among the allotetraploids.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparative genomics of the Primula veris assembly showed that the S locus arose through several gene duplications at different times and separate gene translocations.
statements.evidence: we demonstrated that the S-locus evolved via multiple, asynchronous gene duplications and independent gene translocations
statements.note: The abstract states that the S locus evolved via multiple, asynchronous gene duplications and independent gene translocations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Heterostyly supergenes in other angiosperm families share the molecular architecture of the Primula S locus.
statements.evidence: Is the molecular architecture of heterostyly supergenes across angiosperms similar to that of Primula?
statements.note: The abstract poses this only as an open question for future research and gives no answer either way.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study proposes that S-locus hemizygosity originated via nonhomologous recombination involving two newly discovered pairs of CFB genes that flank the locus.
statements.evidence: We also propose a mechanism for the origin of S-locus hemizygosity via nonhomologous recombination involving the newly discovered two pairs of CFB genes flanking the S locus.
statements.note: The abstract proposes that S-locus hemizygosity arose by nonhomologous recombination involving two newly discovered pairs of flanking CFB genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Primula veris S locus carries only slight signs of degeneration, matching expectations for a hemizygous supergene.
statements.evidence: Finally, we detected only weak signatures of degeneration in the S locus, as predicted for hemizygous supergenes.
statements.note: The abstract reports only weak signatures of degeneration in the S locus, as predicted for hemizygous supergenes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Social spider species have smaller genomes than closely related solitary spider species.
statements.evidence: To identify genomic changes associated with this transition, we compare the genomes of 22 spider species representing eight recent and independent origins of sociality.
statements.note: The genomes were compared for selection shifts and rates of molecular evolution; the abstract reports nothing about genome size.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In spiders, genes showing selection shifts during the transition to sociality include ones previously linked to animal social behavior and to human behavioral disorders.
statements.evidence: These genes are associated with several key functions, such as neurogenesis, behavior, and metabolism, and include genes that previously have been implicated in animal social behavior and human behavioral disorders.
statements.note: The abstract states that these genes include ones previously implicated in animal social behavior and human behavioral disorders.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Social spider species had higher genome-wide rates of molecular evolution, tied to relaxed selection following a drop in effective population size.
statements.evidence: In addition, social species have elevated genome-wide rates of molecular evolution associated with relaxed selection caused by reduced effective population size.
statements.note: The abstract reports elevated genome-wide rates of molecular evolution in social species, associated with relaxed selection from reduced effective population size.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across the repeated transitions from solitary to social life in spiders, hundreds of genes showed shifts in selection.
statements.evidence: Hundreds of genes tend to experience shifts in selection during the repeated transition to social life.
statements.note: The abstract states that hundreds of genes tend to experience shifts in selection during the repeated transition to social life.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with hummingbird-pollinated Costus species, bee-pollinated Costus species emit more floral scent.
statements.evidence: We show that hummingbird-pollinated species have mostly lost their floral scent, whereas bee-pollinated species exhibit either floral scent maintenance or, in some cases, gains of more diverse scent profiles.
statements.note: The abstract states that hummingbird-pollinated species have mostly lost floral scent, whereas bee-pollinated species maintain it or gain more diverse profiles.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Hummingbird-pollinated Costus species produce more nectar than bee-pollinated Costus species.
statements.evidence: These pollinator transitions are accompanied by predictable morphological and color changes, but the changes in floral scent have not been described.
statements.note: The abstract mentions morphological, color and scent changes with pollinator transitions but says nothing about nectar.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Floral scent loss in Costus is attributed to downregulation of genes rather than to their pseudogenization.
statements.evidence: We find the floral scent loss appears to be due to gene downregulation rather than pseudogenization.
statements.note: The abstract attributes floral scent loss to gene downregulation rather than pseudogenization.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study characterized floral scent composition in 30 Costus species sampled across the phylogeny of the genus.
statements.evidence: In this study, we describe the floral scent composition of 30 species of Costus sampled across the phylogeny
statements.note: The abstract states that floral scent composition was described for 30 Costus species sampled across the phylogeny.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Repeated bursts of a handful of highly active retrotransposon families were the main force shaping the genomic and epigenomic features of chicory.
statements.evidence: We achieved a nearly complete chicory genome assembly and found that continuous bursts of a few highly active retrotransposon families largely shaped the (epi)genomic characteristics.
statements.note: The abstract states that continuous bursts of a few highly active retrotransposon families largely shaped the (epi)genomic characteristics of chicory.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparative genomics indicated that fructan accumulation evolved convergently in angiosperms, driven by changes at critical sites of fructan-active enzymes.
statements.evidence: indicated that the fructan-accumulating trait resulted from convergent evolution in angiosperms due to shifts in critical sites of fructan-active enzymes
statements.note: The abstract states that the fructan-accumulating trait resulted from convergent evolution due to shifts in critical sites of fructan-active enzymes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The chicory genome is heavily methylated and has a distinctive three-dimensional structure.
statements.evidence: The highly methylated genome with its unique 3D structure potentially influences critical biological processes.
statements.note: The abstract describes the chicory genome as highly methylated with a unique 3D structure.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In chicory, genes encoding fructan-active enzymes are more highly expressed in roots than in leaves.
statements.evidence: As a major source of industrial fructans (especially inulin-type), chicory (Cichorium intybus L.) is a model species for studying fructan biosynthesis.
statements.note: The abstract reports no tissue-level expression data for fructan-active enzymes, so the root-versus-leaf comparison is neither made nor refuted.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: H4K16ac-based dosage compensation evolved convergently in Artemia franciscana, a crustacean in which females are the heterogametic (ZW) sex.
statements.evidence: By sampling multiple arthropods, we find the convergent evolution of H4K16ac for DC in a female-heterogametic (ZW) species, the crustacean Artemia franciscana.
statements.note: The abstract reports convergent evolution of H4K16ac for dosage compensation in the female-heterogametic crustacean Artemia franciscana.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aged Artemia franciscana individuals showed increased variability in local acetylation on the female Z chromosome, together with disrupted H4K16ac territories.
statements.evidence: In aged individuals, we observe an overall decline in nuclear organization, disrupted H4K16ac territories and increased variability in local acetylation levels on the female Z chromosome.
statements.note: The abstract reports disrupted H4K16ac territories and increased variability in local acetylation levels on the female Z chromosome in aged individuals.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Experimentally lowering H4K16ac levels in Artemia franciscana females shortened their lifespan.
statements.evidence: Our findings shed light on the evolutionary diversity of DC across species and raise the possibility of sex-specific histone acetylation contributing to male-female differences in lifespan.
statements.note: The abstract only raises the possibility that sex-specific acetylation affects lifespan; it reports no experiment that manipulates H4K16ac.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CUT&Tag profiling showed that in Artemia franciscana females, H4K16ac is restricted to the non-recombining stratum of the Z chromosome.
statements.evidence: CUT&Tag analysis demonstrates that H4K16ac is confined to the non-recombining stratum of the Z chromosome in females.
statements.note: The abstract states that CUT&Tag shows H4K16ac confined to the non-recombining stratum of the Z chromosome in females.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The higher gene-loss rates seen in some parasites were almost always shared with their free-living relatives.
statements.evidence: Further, the accelerated rates of gene loss seen in some parasites were almost always shared with their free-living relatives, indicating that the increased rate of loss preceded the rise of parasitism.
statements.note: The abstract states that accelerated gene-loss rates in some parasites were almost always shared with free-living relatives, so they preceded parasitism.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Across the parasites studied, DNA-repair genes were lost at higher rates than housekeeping genes.
statements.evidence: Therefore, the convergent ecological strategies and adaptations that have arisen in distantly related parasitic lineages overlay contingent gene losses, which largely reflect their phylogenetic history.
statements.note: The abstract reports gene losses overall but never compares loss rates between DNA-repair, housekeeping and regulatory genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study characterized housekeeping, regulatory and DNA-repair gene complements in 48 bilaterian species, 20 of them parasites spanning 6 phyla.

statements.note: The abstract states that 48 bilaterian species were characterized, including 20 parasites from 6 different bilaterian phyla.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Parasites following different parasitic strategies showed no strategy-specific pace or pattern of gene loss.
statements.evidence: We found that different parasitic strategies do not display characteristic tempos or modes of gene loss.
statements.note: The abstract states that different parasitic strategies do not display characteristic tempos or modes of gene loss.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Wasp species that lost vitellogenin lay fewer eggs than wasp species that retained the gene.
statements.evidence: In parasitoid wasps, a megadiverse group of hymenopteran insects, yolk protein reduction or loss has been observed in many species, likely linked to the transition from ectoparasitism to endoparasitism.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the hymenopteran genomes analyzed, the vitellogenin gene (Vg) was lost in five independent events across four families, involving 23 endoparasitoid species.
statements.evidence: The conserved insect yolk protein gene vitellogenin ( Vg ) underwent five independent loss events in four families, involving 23 of the analyzed endoparasitoid species.
statements.note: The abstract reports five independent Vg loss events in four families, involving 23 of the analyzed endoparasitoid species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Whole-genome alignments pointed to vitellogenin having been lost during genome rearrangement events.
statements.evidence: Whole-genome alignment suggested that Vg loss occurred during genome rearrangement events.
statements.note: The abstract states that whole-genome alignment suggested Vg loss occurred during genome rearrangement events.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study found that the switch from ectoparasitism to endoparasitism was not the main driver of vitellogenin loss or of later VgR evolution.
statements.evidence: The ectoparasitism to endoparasitism transition did not appear to be the primary driver of Vg loss or the subsequent VgR evolution.
statements.note: The abstract states that the ectoparasitism-to-endoparasitism transition did not appear to be the primary driver of Vg loss or subsequent VgR evolution.
